thread_title: S. oreophila sand Mountain clone B
breadcrumb: S. oreophila sand Mountain clone B

posts.body_html:
Well, technically, this is S. oreophila var. ornata 'Sand Mountain' clone B, but there wasn't enough space to put that in the subject title.

Here's a clone that colors up nicely during mid to late summer. Like many other oreophilas from the sand Mountain region in Alabama, this clone can be heavily veined and beautifully colored in the throat. I'm beginning to wonder how many of your "plain and ordinary" looking oreophilas can display this great color in some years and be a boring solid green in other years. For certain, S. oreophila intrigues me because of it's "chameleon" like ability to have different phenotypes or physical appearances under various different environmental conditions.

Anyhow, here's S. oreophila Sand Mountain clone B under various different light to give perspective:













Look at how the red is bright and intense in full sun. This is how it looks when you see it in person (in full sun of course):

posts.body_html:
Pictures taken late August, 2012. Surprisingly, there's not as much red in the throat-usually, this clone is more colorful later in the season. Also, the shape of this trap is a bit atypical...seems like there's a lot of environmental factors affecting the physical appearance. In any case, the veination is still rather pronounced:


The light affects what we can see-this is the same trap as the previous photo, but there's more red visible in the throat:






Nice pronounced veination:

Hi Calen

I believe perlite is in effect inert and has a PH of 7 ish, so I would doubt that it was that, that held the colours back, perhaps the dilution of acidity in the mix due to the perlite?

Cheers
